docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• Account Module - Provides account and profile management functionalities for MSFLib-based applications.
  • Auth Module - Documentation for MSFLib's authentication and authorization functionalities, including token lifecycle and Google OAuth integration.
  • Workspace Notifications Module - Details the functionalities, integration, and setup of the Workspace Notifications module in FastAPI/MSFLib.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Account module is a comprehensive system designed to integrate account management and profile services within applications built on MSFLib. It provides various endpoints and configurable options for user account interactions, enhancing both user and admin experiences.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Authenticated User Endpoints: /account endpoints for actions like viewing and updating the current user account.
  • Open Registration: Configurable sign-up options that are optional and can be customized per requirements.
  • Admin Management: /admin/accounts endpoints to perform admin-level account creations and modifications.
  • Profile Services: /profiles endpoints for managing user profiles, including uploading avatars.
  • Nested Profile Creation: Option for simultaneous profile creation during account registration.
  • Action Classes: Built-in logic processing with AccountAction and ProfileAction for managing core business functions.

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text:
This module can be installed using Poetry with git dependencies, and it supports different versions of Pydantic:

For Pydantic v2 (recommended):

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-account = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/account", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Here's a basic setup for including the Account module routers into your application:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.account.router import account_router, account_admin_router, profile_router

app = FastAPI()

# User account and profile management
app.include_router(
    account_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

# Admin account management
app.include_router(
    account_admin_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        role_check=role_check,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

# Profile services
app.include_router(
    profile_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        get_current_active_account=get_current_active_account,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

docs.title: Account Endpoints (/account)
docs.text:
• GET /me: Retrieve current authenticated account details.
  • POST /open: Open registration endpoint, customizable path for sign-ups (when enabled).
  • PUT /me: Update details of the current account.
  • POST /verify-availability: Check availability for email, username, or phone.

docs.title: Admin Account Endpoints (/admin/accounts)
docs.text:
• GET /: List all accounts (admin-only access).
  • POST /: Create a new account (admin-only access).
  • PUT /{account_id}: Update an account by ID (admin-only access).
  • GET /{account_id}: Fetch details for a specific account by ID.

docs.title: Profile Endpoints (/profiles)
docs.text:
• GET /: Retrieve profile for the current session's account.
  • GET /{account_id}: Retrieve profiles by specific account ID.
  • POST /: Create or comprehensively update the current profile.
  • PUT /: Update fields within the current profile.
  • PUT /avatar: Upload or change the avatar for the current profile.

docs.title: Configuration and Custom Schemas
docs.text:
Schema Augmentation: Customize validation schemas for registration endpoints using account_create_type to enhance or override the default models used for new accounts.

Here's an example of integrating custom models:

from myapp.schemas import CustomAccountCreate

app.include_router(
    account_router(
        account_create_type=CustomAccountCreate,
        ...
    )
)

app.include_router(
    account_admin_router(
        account_create_type=CustomAccountCreate,
        ...
    )
)

docs.title: Events and Testing
docs.text:
Events: This module emits certain events which can be subscribed to, supporting actions like 'account-created' or 'profile-updated'.

Testing: Execute tests suitable for this module by running:

./scripts/test.sh modules/account/msflib/account/tests

docs.title: Settings and State Management
docs.text:
Configuration for account behavior, including registration options and initial superuser setup, are managed within a settings scope specific to ACCOUNT.

By utilizing this module, applications can efficiently administer both user-facing and administrative account tasks with flexibility and ease of customization.

docs.title: Auth Module
docs.text: The MSFLib Auth module provides comprehensive functionalities for authentication and authorization within FastAPI applications, enabling developers to manage token lifecycles and integrate Google OAuth seamlessly.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The Auth module includes:

  • Login and Access Token Issuance: Initiate user sessions with tokens for authenticated requests.
  • Token Revocation: Implement logout capabilities by invalidating tokens.
  • Password Recovery and Reset Flows: Facilitate password recovery and reset processes.
  • Optional Google OAuth Login and Callback: Integrate with Google Accounts for user login, available upon configuration.
  • Authorization Dependency Factories: Configure account-level and workspace-level access controls using FastAPI dependency factories.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
To install the module, use the following configuration based on your Pydantic version:

For Pydantic v2:

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-auth = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/auth", rev = "dev" }

For Pydantic v1:

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
pydantic = "^1.10"
pydantic-settings = "^1.10"

msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "core-v0.1.1" }
msflib-auth = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/auth", rev = "auth-v0.1.1" }

Refer to the core README for Pydantic Version Compatibility.

docs.title: 1) Set Up Dependencies
docs.text:
Define account and user dependencies:

from msflib.auth.deps import get_account_dependencies, get_user_dependencies
from msflib.auth.resolvers import PathParameterResolver

account_deps = get_account_dependencies(
    AccountModel=Account,
    oauth_token_url="/api/v1/auth/login",
    secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,
    session_dep=get_session,
    keystore_dep=get_keystore,
)

user_deps = get_user_dependencies(
    UserModel=WorkspaceUser,
    WorkspaceModel=Workspace,
    session_dep=get_session,
    account_dependencies=account_deps,
    workspace_resolver=PathParameterResolver(),
)

docs.title: 2) Mount Authorization Routes
docs.text:
Include authentication routes in your FastAPI app:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.auth.router import router as auth_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(
    auth_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_keystore=get_keystore,
        get_current_account=account_deps.get_current_account,
        account_type=Account,
        account_read_type=AccountRead,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/auth",
    )
)

docs.title: Public API Endpoints (/auth)
docs.text:
The module exposes the following authentication endpoints under the /auth route:

  • POST /login
  • GET /google/login (enabled per configuration)
  • POST /google/callback (enabled per configuration)
  • POST /password-recovery
  • POST /verify-token
  • POST /reset-password
  • DELETE /logout

docs.title: Google OAuth Integration
docs.text:
Google OAuth flow is supported by default, allowing frontend applications to pass and validate payloads during OAuth processes using a Pydantic model:

from pydantic import BaseModel

class GoogleAuthPayload(BaseModel):
    # Define the payload structure here

By injecting auth_payload_type during router creation, developers can enforce strict validation of incoming Google OAuth data.

This documentation outlines the key features and setup for using the Auth module within MSFLib, providing a robust solution for authentication needs in FastAPI applications.

docs.title: Workspace Notifications Module
docs.text: The Workspace Notifications module provides essential functionalities for managing and integrating workspace-specific notifications within a FastAPI application using MSFLib. This module is structured to offer a reusable scaffold for notification-related features, enabling both user and admin user notification handling.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
The module is organized as follows:

modules/
└── workspace_notifications/
    ├── pyproject.toml
    ├── README.md
    └── msflib/workspace_notifications/
        ├── __init__.py
        ├── config.py
        ├── actions.py
        ├── router.py
        ├── models/
        ├── service/
        └── tests/
            ├── conftest.py
            └── test_router.py

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: To integrate this module into your project, follow the installation steps based on your Pydantic version:

docs.title: For Pydantic v2 (recommended):
docs.text:
Add the dependencies to your pyproject.toml:

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-workspace-notifications = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/workspace_notifications", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: For Pydantic v1 (legacy):
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
pydantic = "^1.10"
pydantic-settings = "^1.10"

msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "core-v0.1.1" }
msflib-workspace-notifications = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/workspace_notifications", rev = "workspace_notifications-v0.1.0" }

Refer to the Pydantic Version Compatibility for migration guidance.

Install the packages using Poetry:

poetry add msflib msflib-workspace-notifications

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
To start using the module, you can include its routers in your FastAPI application:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.workspace_notifications.router import (
    admin_user_notification_router,
    user_notification_router,
)

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(
    user_notification_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_user=get_current_user,
        get_current_workspace=get_current_workspace,
        prefix="/workspace_notifications/user",
        tags=["workspace_notifications"],
    )
)

app.include_router(
    admin_user_notification_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_user=get_current_user,
        get_current_workspace=get_current_workspace,
        admin_role_check=admin_role_check,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/workspace_notifications/admin",
        tags=["workspace_notifications", "admin"],
    )
)

Configuration settings for the module are accessed using:

settings.scope("WS_NOTIFICATIONS")

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: To execute tests for this module, ensure you are at the repository root and that all dependencies are installed. If you are using the project virtual environment, activate it first with source .venv/bin/activate.
